default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1328.title: Regression-channel edge fade
E-1328.hypothesis: Price far outside the rolling least-squares channel (fit +/- k residual sd) has outrun its own trend line; momentum chasers and stop orders are exhausted and liquidity providers revert it toward the fitted line.

E-1329.title: Point-scale excursion fade
E-1329.hypothesis: A move of 150+ index points in minutes is as large as the trade stop/target scale; scalpers take profit and stops sit behind it, so a bar closing against the excursion starts a give-back.

E-1330.title: Index-with-dollar co-move anomaly fade
E-1330.hypothesis: The index normally moves against the dollar; when both are up (or both down) from the open the index move is not backed by the usual currency channel and is fragile, so fade the index.

E-1331.title: Post-narrow-day range break
E-1331.hypothesis: After a session whose range was below average, volatility tends to expand the next day (range clustering); a close through the recent high/low on such a day is the start of that expansion, so follow it.

E-1332.title: VWAP-band dwell departure
E-1332.hypothesis: Price glued to the session VWAP for a long time means two-sided benchmark trading in balance; the first close leaving the band is the side that has won initiative, so follow the departure.

E-1333.title: Counter-burst in the day's trend
E-1333.hypothesis: On a day trading on one side of VWAP and the open, a sharp burst against the day's side is mostly stop-run and small-trader flow; trend holders absorb it, so trade back with the day's side.

E-1334.title: Alternating-colour chop break
E-1334.hypothesis: A run of bars alternating up and down is a rotation where each side's market orders cancel; the first close beyond the chop's range means one side ran out of orders, so follow the break.

E-1335.title: Index-in-dollar-terms z-score fade
E-1335.hypothesis: The index divided by the dollar (index in USD) is the foreign investor's price; when it stretches from its recent mean, arbitrage and relative-value desks trade it back, and the index leg reverts.

E-1336.title: Previous-hour close-location carry
E-1336.hypothesis: Desks and algos that work parent orders by clock hour continue into the next hour when the last hour closed near its high (low); at each hour start follow that close location.

E-1337.title: Donchian-midline cross
E-1337.hypothesis: The midpoint of the fast channel crossing the midpoint of a slower channel (Ichimoku tenkan/kijun logic) marks a shift of the trading range's centre that trend followers using it act on together; follow it.
